sections.heading: context
sections.markdown: MONTHLY_IC 2026-09-05. IDX agri/CPO names were killed while the commodity complex re-rated around them. War-premium tape intact (Brent ~95.9). Two of the three source kills carried valuation reason_tags; one carried process.

sections.heading: belief
sections.markdown: "Expensive on its own numbers" was judged from the name's own P&L / spot earnings, without carrying the commodity/energy complex and the macro tilt (CPO/agri complex, energy spot, war premium) inside the valuation frame.

sections.heading: outcome
sections.markdown: Kills avoided ~zero loss and left large gains: DSNG.JK 07-13 valuation +39.0%; TAPG.JK 08-19 valuation +21.9%; LSIP.JK 07-22 process +25.7%. The names re-rated with the complex after being killed.

sections.heading: cause
sections.markdown: `thesis_wrong` — valuation frame anchored to the name's own numbers while the commodity complex and macro regime were re-rating above them. The through-cycle marker was not re-set when the complex moved.

sections.heading: rule
sections.markdown: Value IDX agri/CPO names with the commodity-complex and macro tilt inside the valuation frame (spot, war premium), not the name's own P&L alone; a name re-rating with the complex is not "expensive on its own numbers."

sections.heading: evidence
sections.markdown:
- T-INDO-DSNG-001 (2026-07-13, valuation, px_at_kill 1180) — counterfactual +39.0%
- T-INDO-TAPG-001 (2026-08-19, valuation, px_at_kill 1830) — counterfactual +21.9%
- T-INDO-LSIP-001 (2026-07-22, process, px_at_kill 1340) — counterfactual +25.7%
- LSIP's kill was process (pipeline-integrity) and stands as a process kill; it is not reversed by this rule. The rule's change-the-outcome anchors are the two valuation kills (DSNG, TAPG). The same complex-frame applies to IDX energy names under a sustained war premium (Brent ~95.9) — observable future trigger: an IDX commodity-linked name re-rating with the complex while its own P&L is flat.
